summary: Douglas FPA lookout site east of Days Creek, in use since 1942; the cab on a recycled steel tower is on emergency status and was boarded up on a 2015 visit.

facts.design: 14 x 14 Amort-style flat-roof cab on a recycled 20-foot steel tower

access.note: Listed as accessible to the public, but the cab is on emergency status and was boarded up on a 2015 visit. The approach is a gated BLM spur road.

visit.trail_note: From Days Creek Road, drive 2.3 miles on BLM Road 7.0 to a gated spur road, then walk about half a mile uphill (2015 visit).

events.note: Supplementary lookout planned for Bland Mountain by the Douglas FPA
Site established with a tent camp; a 1944 report says the site had been used as a lookout for three years and the man there had lived in a tent
14 x 14 cab on a timber tower; the register says 25 feet, Forest Lookouts says 20 feet
Cab lowered and remounted on a recycled 20-foot steel water tower; sources give 1996 or 1997

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The site was in use from 1942 with a tent camp. The 14 x 14 cab on a timber tower dates to 1947, which is the register's built year. Heights for that 1947 tower still differ: 25 feet in the register, 20 feet in Forest Lookouts.

sources.title: Bland Mountain, Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: Current status conflicts: the register describes the Douglas association staffing it, while firelookout.com says emergency status and the 2015 visit found it not regularly staffed and boarded up. The 1996 vs 1997 remount date is unresolved. Elevation: record 784.6 m matches the register's 2,574 ft; firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 2,696 ft. Record height 6.1 m vs present 20 ft 4 in (6.2 m) is a small difference, so no correction is proposed. Staffing as_of is undated. Visit route comes from a 2015 blog visit; recheck before publishing any visit advice.
